summary: RTC battery replacement caused clock drift and Intune SCEP enrollment failures on Lenovo X13s after depot SSD swap
description: Issue summary: Several Lenovo X13s returned from depot SSD replacement were failing to complete Intune automatic enrollment. Impact: blocked workstation provisioning for 7 devices on the week of 2026-02-16, delaying rollout to new hires. Root cause hypothesis: RTC (real-time clock) battery replacement performed during depot repair left system time incorrect (multiple years in the past) which caused SCEP certificate requests to be rejected by the CA due to excessive time skew, and Intune enrollment to fail with certificate validation errors. Environment: Depot-imaged Windows 11 23H2 image, company provisioning image v2026-02, Intune AutoPilot / SCEP flow, devices returned from depot with SSD swap and platform firmware updated to vendor-repackaged image. This ticket tracks investigation, temporary mitigation, and runbook updates.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Perform depot SSD replacement and standard firmware/driver reflash flow used by depot (model: Lenovo X13s).
2) Run provisioning image that triggers Autopilot/Intune SCEP enrollment during OOBE.
3) Observe enrollment fail at 'Device Management' step.
4) Check system clock from WinPE or from Windows settings; note clock is set to year 2000-2006 or 1970 depending on UEFI reset.
5) Attempt manual time sync -> successful enrollment proceeds.
investigation_notes:
- Initial triage by depot support (2026-02-18): enrollment failures correlated with devices processed in the same repair batch.
- Support reproduced the issue by intentionally removing RTC coin cell from a test X13s and performing standard repro steps; time reset behavior reproduced.
- SCEP CA logs show CSR rejects with 'certificate request validation failed: clock skew > allowable threshold' and CA responses referencing certificate validity window.
- Intune logs on device show MDM policy download failing with 0x8013141A (certificate validation/time error) and SCEP client returning status indicating CSR denied.
- BIOS versions on affected machines had vendor tool that resets RTC to epoch when coin cell absent; firmware update during depot reflashing did not restore correct time.
- NTP servers are reachable in depot network, but automatic time sync only runs after Intune provisioning completes; thus devices with clock skew > 5 minutes fail SCEP before NTP corrects time.
- Related to depot workflow: imaging automation does not currently enforce post-flash time sanity check or early NTP sync prior to initiating Autopilot/SCEP.
- Hypothesis confirmed: manual time set (or temporary DHCP NTP sync) allowed CSR to validate and enrollment completed successfully.

resolution: Root cause: RTC/time reset after coin-cell replacement and vendor firmware behavior led to time skew that caused SCEP CSR rejections. Resolution: 1) Hotfix imaging change deployed to depot run: force NTP sync (w32tm) immediately after post-flash boot but before starting Intune/SCEP flows. 2) Replaced RTC batteries on affected units and re-ran provisioning; enrollment succeeded. 3) Submitted firmware support case with vendor to request RTC preservation in future firmware builds and updated depot checklist to verify BIOS time. 4) Updated internal runbook 'depot-repair-provisioning-checklist' and added a mandatory 'time sanity check' step. Follow-up actions assigned to depot and firmware owners.
